title: Antisymmetric Difference is 2L-Lipschitz
content: antisymmetric_diff_lipschitz proves that g(x) = f(x) - f(-x) is (L+L)-Lipschitz when f is L-Lipschitz. The proof composes f with negation (LipschitzWith.id.neg, constant 1) to get f(-x) as L-Lipschitz, then uses LipschitzWith.sub.

title: Lipschitz Antipodal Deviation Bound (2L)
content: lipschitz_antipodal_deviation_bound shows |f(x) - f(-x)| <= 2L for L-Lipschitz f and x in [-1,1]. Uses dist(x,-x) = |2x| <= 2 (since |x| <= 1) combined with the Lipschitz bound |f(x)-f(-x)| <= L * dist(x,-x).

title: Bisection Convergence to Zero
content: bisection_width_tendsto_zero proves 2*(1/2)^n -> 0 as n -> infinity. Uses tendsto_pow_atTop_nhds_zero_of_lt_one (for |1/2| < 1) followed by multiplication by the constant 2.

title: Antipodal Deviation Bounded by Oscillation
content: antipodal_deviation_le_oscillation shows |f(x) - f(-x)| <= sup(f) - inf(f) on [-1,1]. Both f(x) and f(-x) are in the image of f on [-1,1] (since x in [-1,1] implies -x in [-1,1] by symmetry), so each lies between inf and sup.

title: Coincidence Set: Nonempty, Compact, Has Minimum
content: coincidence_set_nonempty_compact proves {x in [-1,1] | f(x)=f(-x)} is nonempty (x=0 witness) and compact (closed subset of compact [-1,1], where closedness uses isClosed_eq). coincidence_set_has_inf proves this set has a minimum element via csInf_mem for compact nonempty sets.
mathContext: $C(f) = \{x \in [-1,1] \mid f(x) = f(-x)\}$ is nonempty ($0 \in C$), compact, and has $\inf C \in C$.

title: Circle Antipodal Deviation Bound
content: circle_antipodal_deviation_bound shows |f(cos theta, sin theta) - f(-cos theta, -sin theta)| <= 2L for L-Lipschitz f: R^2 -> R. Key: dist((cos,sin),(-cos,-sin)) = max(|2cos|,|2sin|) <= 2 using the product max-norm.

title: Perturbation Stability (2 epsilon Bound)
content: perturbation_antisymmetric_bound shows |(f(x)-f(-x)) - (g(x)-g(-x))| <= 2*epsilon when |f-g| <= epsilon on [-1,1]. Proof: triangle inequality gives |..| <= |f(x)-g(x)| + |f(-x)-g(-x)| <= epsilon + epsilon.

title: Discrete IVT: Different Endpoints Imply Adjacent Change
content: discrete_ivt proves: if f: Fin(n+2) -> alpha has f(0) != f(last), then there exist adjacent i, i+1 with f(i) != f(i+1). Proof: contrapositive via fin_adjacent_eq_implies_const (if all adjacent agree, function is constant by Fin.induction).
mathContext: If $f(0) \neq f(n+1)$ for $f : \{0,\ldots,n+1\} \to \alpha$, then $\exists i$ with $f(i) \neq f(i+1)$.

title: Tucker's Lemma (1D) with Integer Labels
content: tucker_1d proves: given f: Fin(n+2) -> Z with values in {+-1} and f(0) = -f(last), there exists adjacent i with f(i)+f(i+1) = 0. Step 1: f(0) != f(last) since f(0) = -f(last) and f(last) in {+-1} means negation differs. Step 2: discrete_ivt gives adjacent pair with different values. Step 3: case split on all {+-1} combinations shows different implies sum zero.

title: Tucker-BU Equivalence in 1D
content: tucker_bu_equivalence_1d proves the logical equivalence between BU (continuous odd f has zero in [-1,1]) and Tucker (antipodal {+-1} labeling has complementary edge). Forward: Tucker is independently proved. Backward: x=0 witnesses odd function zero (f(0)=-f(-0)=-f(0) gives 2f(0)=0).
mathContext: $\text{BU}_{1D} \Leftrightarrow \text{Tucker}_{1D}$: continuous odd zeros $\Leftrightarrow$ complementary edges in labeled sequences.

title: Circle Non-Injectivity via IVT
content: circle_noninjectivity proves: for continuous f: R^2 -> R, there exists theta in [0,pi] with f(cos theta, sin theta) = f(-cos theta, -sin theta). This is the circle BU proved directly via IVT on g(theta) = f(cos theta,...) - f(-cos theta,...), using g(pi) = -g(0) from trig identities cos(pi)=-1, sin(pi)=0.
